{{Quote|When my husband&mdash;the captain&mdash;tried to stop them, they killed him. Just shot him.|Gille Narvis, on the killing of her husband Jarl by Toric Bisilt|<ref name="Incursion">{{LivingForce|Belted In: Incursion}}</ref>}}
'''Toric Bisilt''' was a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served as a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] in the [[Thaereian military]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], Bisilt was assigned to customs duty in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]] in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], serving aboard the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[Thaere Runner]]''. When passing near to the [[Cularin comet cloud]], the [[Corvette/Legends|corvette]] encountered a passing [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] by a group of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance operatives]] and Bisilt boarded the vessel to perform a customs inspection.

Bisilt later gained command of the [[DP20 gunship/Legends|Corellian Gunship]] ''[[Thaere Interceptor]]'' and while on patrol in the [[Cularin asteroid belt]], he intercepted and boarded a [[Aggressive Negotiation|freighter]] transporting arms for the [[Cularin Militia]] [[Army/Legends|armed force]]. The Bothan and his [[Soldier/Legends|troops]] seized the vessel's cargo and [[Death/Legends|killed]] the ship's [[Officer/Legends|officers]], then departed and boarded another passing vessel that had been drawn to a [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]] from the stricken [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]].

==Biography==
===Customs duty on the ''Thaere Runner''===
{{Quote|What is your destination?|Lieutenant Toric Bisilt, while inspecting the starship of the heroes of Cularin|<ref name="Outward Bound" />}}
Toric Bisilt was a [[Gender/Legends|Bothan]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], who worked as a [[Customs official/Legends|customs officer]] in the [[Thaereian military]], an [[Army/Legends|armed force]] from the [[Thaereian system]], during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Bisilt held the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] and served aboard the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] ''[[Thaere Runner]]''.<ref name="Outward Bound" /> Around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="date">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure ''[[Below the Belt: Philology]]'' [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten years to the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], ''[[Looking In: Outward Bound]]'' is therefore dated to circa [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].</ref> Bisilt accompanied the [[Corvette/Legends|corvette]] on a customs duty assignment in the [[Cularin system]],<ref name="Outward Bound" /> an [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]]<ref name="LFCG"> ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]''</ref> [[Star system/Legends|star system]] that the [[Thaereian]] military was [[Thaereian Navy charter|chartered]] to defend.<ref name="Outward Bound" />

{{RPG|''[[Looking In: Outward Bound]]''}}
While traveling near to the [[Cularin comet cloud]] on the edge of the [[Cularin/Legends|Cularin]] system, the ''Thaere Runner'' encountered a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] bound for the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Druckenwell/Legends|Druckenwell]] and ordered it to power down for inspection. Bisilt lead a group of [[Thaereian]] [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] onto the vessel and interrogated the crew, a group of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance agents]] transporting goods for the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] entrepreneur [[Renna (Rodian)|Renna]]. Hoping to uncover any contraband that the vessel might be be carrying, Bisilt demanded the [[Agent/Legends|agents]] provide information on the ship's cargo and destination. He also ordered three of the Thaereian soldiers to search the ship for evidence of anything untoward. Once the inspection was complete, Bisilt and the Thaereian soldiers disembarked from the vessel and allowed the freelancers to proceed with their journey.<ref name="Outward Bound" />
{{Endgame}}

===Enforcing the blockade===
{{Quote|I think the highest ranking one was a Lieutenant.|Gille Narvis, describing Toric Bisilt and the Thaereian soldiers who boarded the ''Aggressive Negotiation''|<ref name="Incursion" />}}
The Thaereian military later strengthened their [[Navy/Legends|naval]] presence in the Cularin system and established a [[Blockade of the Cularin system|full blockade]], overtly with a view to deterring [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] but in truth to counter the [[Cularin Militia]], an [[Army/Legends|armed group]] that opposed the Thaereian occupation of the Cularin system. Bisilt was assigned to customs duty in support of the [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]],<ref name="Incursion" /> commanding<ref name="CSWE - Gille Narvis">{{CSWECite|II|361|Narvis, Gille}}</ref> the [[DP20 gunship/Legends|Corellian Gunship]] ''[[Thaere Interceptor]]''.<ref name="Incursion" />

On patrol in the [[Cularin asteroid belt]], the ''Thaere Interceptor'' apprehended the [[Barloz-class medium freighter|''Barloz''-class medium freighter-]] ''[[Aggressive Negotiation]]'', an arms [[Transport/Legends|transport]] carrying weapons for the Cularin Militia, and he ordered the vessel to stop for inspection.<ref name="Incursion" /> Bisilt led<ref name="CSWE - Gille Narvis" /> a Thaereian boarding party onto the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and had his troops confiscate the vessel's arms consignment and destroy the cargo manifest, despite the crew having documentation that proved their haul was legitimate. After the freighter's [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Jarl Narvis]] challenged the seizure,<ref name="Incursion" /> Bisilt shot and [[Death/Legends|killed]] him.<ref name="CSWE - Jarl Narvis">{{CSWECite|II|361|Narvis, Jarl}}</ref> The Thaereians then took the lives of the transport's other [[Officer/Legends|officers]] after they resisted. Before the Thaereians could shoot Narvis' [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Gille Narvis]], Bisilt and his forces were called away to investigate another vessel approaching their position,<ref name="Incursion" /> which had been drawn over by a [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]] sent out by Gille. Bisilt<ref name="CSWE - Gille Narvis" /> and the rest of the boarding party disembarked the freighter, leaving the ''Aggressive Negotiation'' disabled and adrift in [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="Incursion" />

{{RPG|''[[Belted In: Incursion]]''}}
The ''Thaere Interceptor'' caught up with the starship that it had been ordered to intercept, which was [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] by the same freelance operatives that Bisilt had previously encountered<ref name="Incursion" /> when on customs duty aboard the ''Thaere Runner''.<ref name="Outward Bound" /> Accompanied by a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of Thaereian soldiers, Bisilt boarded the vessel and demanded that the [[Captain/Legends|captain]] report to him and provide proper legal documentation regarding the particulars of their ship. The Bothan customs officer did not recognise the freelance agents from his previous run-in with them and questioned them regarding their employers, cargo and destination. Hoping that the vessel might be carrying contraband for the Thaereians to uncover, Bisilt ordered his soldiers to search the ship. Once he was satisfied that everything was in order, Bisilt returned to the ''Thaere Interceptor'' and allowed the freelancers' ship to leave.<ref name="Incursion" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|What are you carrying?|Lieutenant Toric Bisilt, while inspecting the starship of the heroes of Cularin|<ref name="Outward Bound" />}}
Toric Bisilt was an obnoxious and merciless individual who gave customers officers a bad reputation. He relished using physical force against others and was content to shoot those who he saw as a threat.<ref name="Incursion" /> When questioning people in the course of his duties as a customs [[Officer/Legends|officer]], he maintained a business-like demeanor<ref name="Outward Bound" /> and sought to coerce those whose ships he inspected into providing inconsistent answers;<ref name="Incursion" /> truthful responses perplexed and irked him. He would probe any conflicting information provided to him and was determined to find illicit cargo onboard the vessels he inspected.<ref name="Outward Bound" /> He especially sought to put pressure on individuals who remained quiet when he quizzed them, because he considered such people to be trying to conceal something important from him.<ref name="Incursion" />

The Bothan lieutenant expected that others should be deferential toward him, as he saw befitting someone of his rank. He also believed that he deserved better than customs patrol duty and was therefore responsive to the use of flattery to manipulate and deceive him.<ref name="Incursion" /> He had a dislike of members of the Cularin Militia and was wary of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]],<ref name="Outward Bound" /> a [[Monk/Legends|monastic]] [[Jedi Order/Legends|order]] of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]].<ref name="CSWE - Jedi Order">{{CSWECite|II|150|Jedi Order}}</ref>

Bisilt was proficient in the use of a variety of armaments, including [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifles]], [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]], [[heavy weapon]]s and [[Vibro-weapon/Legends|vibroweapon]]s. The Bothan was [[Language/Legends|multi-lingual]] and in addition to [[Galactic Basic Standard|Basic]], he could both speak and [[Writing/Legends|write]] [[Bothese]], and was also fluent in the [[Language/Legends|languages]] [[Caarimala|Caarite]], [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]], [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]] and [[Sullustese/Legends|Sullustan]].<ref name="Outward Bound" />

==Equipment==
While assigned to customs duty in the Cularin system, Bisilt wore a dark [[Color/Legends|blue]] combat [[jumpsuit]] with the [[Gold/Legends|gold]] insignia of the Thaereian military emblazoned on the upper part of each [[Limb/Legends|arm]] and a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] communication device clipped to the collar. He was armed with a [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]], strapped to his left thigh, and he was also equipped with a [[Breath mask/Legends|breath mask]] and [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]].<ref name="Outward Bound" />

==Behind the scenes==
Toric Bisilt first appeared within [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity in the [[2002]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] adventure ''[[Looking In: Outward Bound]]'' by [[Morrie Mullins]] and [[Lee Pickler]], which formed part of the [[Looking In trilogy]] of [[RPGA]]'s [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|Living Force]] campaign.<ref name="Outward Bound" /> He made a further appearance in the Living Force campaign in the [[2003]] adventure ''[[Belted In: Incursion]]'' by [[Jae Walker]] and [[Victor Long]], part of the campaign's [[Belted In trilogy]].<ref name="Incursion" /> Bisilt was also referenced in the [[2008]] compendium ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' in the entries for Gille<ref name="CSWE - Gille Narvis" /> and Jarl Narvis.<ref name="CSWE - Jarl Narvis" />

The ''Encylopedia'' provided clarification regarding Bisilt's participation in the attack on the crew of the ''Aggressive Negotiation''<ref name="CSWE - Jarl Narvis" /> In ''Belted In: Incursion'' it is implied that Bisilt lead the attack, noting that the leader of the Thaereian troops who boarded the freighter was a lieutenant and party of the same group of Thaereians encountered by the freelance operatives a short time after.<ref name="Incursion" /> The ''Encylopedia'' explicitly confirmed Bisilt's role involvement in the attack and provided new information that it was Bisilt himself who killed Jarl Narvis.<ref name="CSWE - Jarl Narvis" />

===Possible roleplaying outcomes===
In ''Looking In: Outward Bound''<ref name="Outward Bound" /> and ''Incursion'',<ref name="Incursion" /> the players roleplay as the freelance agents that the freelance agents that Bisilt encounters while on customs patrol. In ''Outward Bound'', it is possible for the player characters' to be boarded by Bisilt and Thaereian soldiers while departing the Cularin system. Bisilt questions the player characters and is especially watchful of and derisory toward any players roleplaying as members of the Cularin Militia. He also requests that any Jedi or other [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-using player characters refrain from using their [[Force power/Legends|powers]] to perform [[Mind trick/Legends|mind tricks]] on the Thaereian boarding party.<ref name="Outward Bound" />

Once the Thaereians have completed their inspection, Bisilt then allows the player characters to leave. It is alternately possible for the players to engage in combat with Bisilt and the other Thaereians. It is also possible for the player characters to destroy the ''Thaere Runner'', in which case Bisilt and the rest of the corvette's crew are killed.<ref name="Outward Bound" /> This latter eventuality presumably does not form part of official ''[[Star Wars]]'' Legends continuity given that Bisilt subsequently appeared in ''Incursion''<ref name="Incursion" /> and therefore could not have died during the events of ''Outward Bound''.<ref name="Outward Bound" />

In ''Belted In: Incursion'' it is possible for the player characters to encounter Bisilt for a second time, if their ship is apprehended by the ''Thaere Interceptor'' and boarded by the Bothan lieutenant and his forces.<ref name="Incursion" /> As he does in ''Outward Bound'',<ref name="Outward Bound" /> Bisilt warms any Jedi player characters not to perform any mind tricks, though despite his warning is possible for [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-using players to use mind tricks to convince Bisilt to let their freelance agents leave unhindered. When questioning the player characters, Bisilt gives particular focus to challenging any of the players who try to remain quiet, as he suspects them of hiding something from him.<ref name="Incursion" /> Also like in ''Outward Bound''<ref name="Outward Bound" />, it is possible for the freelance agents to engage in combat with Bisilt and his soldiers.<ref name="Incursion" />
